title: Authorization Patterns and Financial Guardrails — Company Ops Playbook
author: Sofia Alvarez
content:
Overview

This playbook defines company-wide operational patterns for authorization, purchasing and expense guardrails, change control, data classification and retention, vendor onboarding, and business travel rules. The objective is to enable efficient day-to-day operations while preserving risk controls, auditability, and predictable approval paths.

Scope

Applies to: all Redwood employees, contractors with company accounts, and business units that initiate procurement, vendor relationships, or system changes. Exceptions are handled through the Exceptions process (see Governance).

Principles

- Least privilege for systems and data; role-based access where possible.
- Separation of duties for approvals over financial thresholds.
- Time-bound access and documented justification for elevated permissions.
- Proportional vendor review based on risk and spend.
- Clear SLOs for access and procurement workflows to reduce operational friction.

1) Access & Permissions

Goal: Fast, auditable access provisioning with risk-calibrated approvals.

Roles and responsibilities:
- Requestor: Submits access request with business justification and expected duration.
- Manager: Verifies job need and approves low-medium risk requests.
- System Owner (service owner): Confirms access scope and approves.
- InfoSec: Approves access to Confidential/Restricted data or privileged infra.

Access classification and SLOs:
- Low-risk (read-only, public/internal data): fulfillment SLO 24 business hours.
- Medium-risk (write permissions, non-production infra): fulfillment SLO 48 business hours.
- High-risk (production admin, Confidential/Restricted data): fulfillment SLO 72 business hours + InfoSec review.
- Emergency access: documented emergency request, <8 hours review window; must be revoked and post-reviewed within 3 business days.

Approval paths (examples):
1. Developer requests read access to analytics dashboard (Low-risk) -> Manager approve -> Automated provisioning.
2. SRE requests production kube-admin (High-risk) -> Manager + System Owner + InfoSec -> Time-limited token via PAM.

Provisioning patterns:
- Role templates: use pre-defined role templates (engineering-read, engineering-write, infra-operator) to minimize bespoke grants.
- Time-boxed grants: default 30 days for temporary elevated access unless extended with renewed justification.
- PAM integration: all production admin activity must go through privileged access management tooling with session recording where available.

2) Change Management

Purpose: Control risk from code, infra, and configuration changes while enabling frequent safe delivery.

Change categories:
- Standard (pre-authorized routine changes): scheduled, low impact. No CAB approval required.
- Normal (non-emergency changes): require change ticket, testing evidence, and CAB review for higher-risk changes.
- Emergency: expedited review path; post-implementation review mandatory.

Process:
1. Create change ticket in Jira with owner, rollback plan, test artifacts, and monitoring playbook.
2. Run automated pre-flight checks (unit tests, integration smoke, canary gates).
3. If categorized Normal and impact > medium, include CAB review. CAB meets weekly; emergency CAB convenes ad-hoc.
4. Implement staged rollout: dev -> canary -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with health checks and automatic rollback on failure thresholds.

Risk thresholds and gating:
- Any change that impacts data classification boundaries (e.g., changes to KMS usage, S3 bucket ACLs) requires Security sign-off.
- Rollback trigger: >1% error rate increase sustained for 5 minutes, or >25% latency regression for two consecutive monitoring windows.

3) Data Management

Classification levels:
- PUBLIC: intended for public release. No special controls.
- INTERNAL: company-internal information; avoid public disclosure.
- CONFIDENTIAL: personal data, customer data, PII, sensitive business info. Requires encryption at rest and in transit.
- RESTRICTED: highest-risk material (regulated financial records, legal investigations, unreleased M&A data). Access by explicit approval only.

Retention & archival:
- HR records: 7 years (HR must request archive with retention justification).
- Financial records: 7 years for audit.
- Product telemetry: default 1 year unless product team declares longer retention for analytics (requires Data Steward approval).
- Backups and logs: 90 days hot, 2 years cold archive unless restricted by regulatory requirements.

Encryption & keys:
- All CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data must be encrypted at rest using company KMS.
- Customer keys (where offered) must be managed via customer-provided KMS or HSM integration.

Data movement and allowed regions:
- Default storage is in approved cloud regions (US, EU regions listed in the region whitelist). Transfers outside approved regions require Data Steward sign-off and legal review.

Data access auditability:
- All accesses to CONFIDENTIAL/RESTRICTED data must be logged and retained for at least 2 years for audit.

4) Procurement & Expenses

Approval matrix (monetary thresholds):
- <$2,500: Card purchase or manager approval.
- $2,500–$25,000: Manager + Finance team approval (purchase request in procurement system).
- $25,001–$250,000: Manager + Finance + Procurement team + Legal (contract review).
- >$250,000: Executive sponsor sign-off (VP/Head) + Procurement + Legal + Finance.

Procurement steps:
1. Complete Purchase Request form with business justification, supplier, SOW/quote, expected dates.
2. Procurement evaluates supplier risk and competitive alternatives.
3. Legal reviews contracts for liabilities, IP, and data protection clauses.
4. Finance approves budget and issues PO.

Payment and invoicing:
- Standard invoice terms: net 30 unless negotiated.
- Finance will not process invoices without matching PO and receiving confirmation unless pre-approved.
- For subscriptions, vendor must provide annual SOW and renewal notice 60 days before renewal.

Expense policy highlights:
- Personal card reimbursements: submit receipts within 30 days; expenses older than 90 days require justification and may be declined.
- Per-diem: domestic $75/day for meals, international $85/day unless local per-diem schedule applies.
- Lodging caps: domestic standard rate $250/night, high-cost market (SF, NYC, LON) cap $350/night with manager pre-approval.
- Ground transportation: preference for ride-share or public transit when practical; car rentals require justification.

5) Vendor Management & Onboarding

Risk tiers and review requirements:
- Tier 1 (Low-risk, < $25k annual): standard onboarding, SIG-Lite questionnaire.
- Tier 2 (Medium-risk, $25k–$250k or access to INTERNAL/CONFIDENTIAL data): full security questionnaire, basic financial viability check, contract review.
- Tier 3 (High-risk, > $250k or access to RESTRICTED data): SOC 2 Type II or equivalent, penetration test evidence, security addendum, and board-level review for strategic vendors.

Onboarding checklist:
1. Business Sponsor submits Vendor Intake form (name, scope, expected spend, data types).
2. Procurement assigns risk tier and issues vendor questionnaire.
3. Security evaluates responses; request additional controls if necessary.
4. Legal negotiates contract and SOW.
5. Procurement issues PO and records vendor in vendor registry.
6. Vendor access provisioning is time-limited and monitored; credentials are rotated on a schedule.

Contractual guardrails:
- Standard data processing agreement (DPA) mandatory for any vendor processing personal or customer data.
- Insurance: minimum commercial general liability and cyber insurance coverage required for Tier 2+.

Offboarding:
- At contract termination: procurement triggers offboarding checklist including account termination, data return/destruction certification, and license revocation.

6) Travel Policy & Expense Templates

Booking and approvals:
- Travel must be booked with corporate travel portal or approved agency for insurance coverage.
- International travel requires manager and Security brief for high-risk countries (see travel whitelist/blacklist).

Expense submission cadence:
- Submit expenses within 30 days of travel completion. Finance reviews and processes within 10 business days after submission when complete.

Personal travel combined with business: must clearly separate business expenses and non-reimbursable personal costs.

Travel safety & insurance:
- Company travel insurance covers medical evacuation and emergency assistance for approved business travel.
- Travelers must register trips with Security prior to departure for visits to high-risk regions.

7) Templates and Forms (links)

- Access Request Form: /confluence/templates/access-request-form (use this for all access grants).
- Purchase Request Form: /confluence/templates/purchase-request-form (mandatory for > $2,500).
- Vendor Intake & Risk Assessment: /confluence/templates/vendor-intake-risk.
content_continued:
- Travel Expense Template: /confluence/templates/travel-expense-template
- Change Ticket Template (Jira): project=CHG, include fields: owner, rollback plan, health-checks, monitoring links.

8) Governance, Ownership and Exceptions

Ownership:
- Finance owns procurement policies and approval matrix maintenance.
- Security owns data classification, KMS policies and vendor security requirements.
- People-ops and Legal support travel and contract policies respectively.

Exception process:
- Submit an Exception Request with rationale, compensating controls, duration, and owner.
- Exceptions are reviewed by a cross-functional committee monthly. High-risk exceptions (>90 days or involving RESTRICTED data) require executive sponsor and Legal approval.

Audit and continuous improvement:
- Quarterly audits of procurement spend against PO compliance.
- Annual vendor risk re-assessment for Tier 2/3 vendors.
- Post-incident reviews are required for any access, change, or vendor incident impacting Confidential/Restricted data.

Appendix: Quick-reference tables

Monetary approval quick table:
| Amount | Approver chain | Notes |
|-------:|----------------|-------|
| <$2,500 | Manager | Card purchase allowed |
| $2,500–$25,000 | Manager + Finance | PO recommended |
| $25,001–$250,000 | Manager + Procurement + Legal + Finance | Contract review required |
| >$250,000 | Exec sponsor + Procurement + Legal + Finance | Board-level approval for strategic spend possible |

Data classification quick table:
- PUBLIC: no controls
- INTERNAL: RBAC + audit logs
- CONFIDENTIAL: Encryption + KMS + logging
- RESTRICTED: Explicit approval + limited audience + legal oversight

Contact and escalation
- Procurement: procurement@redwood.example.com
- Finance: finance@redwood.example.com
- InfoSec: security@redwood.example.com
- Security Operations (urgent): #sec-ops or pager on-call

Revision history

Notes
- This playbook is intended to be a living document. Teams should propose changes via PR into the policies repository or by filing a Governance suggestion in the PULSE board.
